record.file_problem: The input contains the README and file list only; the code and results files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports applying the difference-in-means refusal direction and projection ablation, following the cited method, to a model after inoculation training and reports refusal outcomes.
record.gate_note: The README reports direction alignment and ablation/refusal outcomes. The listed files include results.json and a plot, but their contents are not available here. The reported ASR values are included in row notes as the complement of refusal rates, rather than separate rows.
record.test_reason: The repo fits Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means direction and applies projection ablation to Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, before and after an inoculation LoRA fine-tune. It reports refusal rates on 10 harmful prompts, so it tests the ablation part of V1 and cross-checkpoint transfer (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors add that inoculation is a behavioural rather than mechanistic defense: the refusal representation is essentially untouched, so the stale base direction jailbreaks the defended model 10/10.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the cited difference-in-means direction and projection-subtraction mechanism, but focuses on inoculation versus ablation and reports the attack at the selected layer 14. This is a composition experiment repo, not a standalone replication repo.
record.method_sensitivity: The attack evaluation uses layer 14, selected as the best layer in the cited sweep. Direction fitting uses 32 harmful and 32 harmless prompts; evaluation uses 10 direct-harmful prompts. The inoculation system prompt is used during training only, not inference.
record.problems: The README reports one seed, one model, one inoculation defense, and one attack layer. It notes the direction fit uses only 64 prompts and the evaluation only 10 prompts; no uncertainty estimates are given. Other capabilities are not evaluated. Results are reported in the README, but the listed results.json and plot were not available for inspection.
record.rows_left_out: No reported refusal conditions were left out. ASR values are stated in row notes rather than separate rows because they are reported as the complement of refusal rates.

untested.parts: Inducing refusal by adding the direction; preservation of other abilities. Only 10 prompts at one layer.
Transfer across languages, unrelated models, or from base to instruct models. Only a LoRA fine-tune of the same instruct model is tested.

tranche.reason: It uses Arditi et al.'s difference-in-means direction from 32+32 prompts, all-layer projection ablation during generation, and the refusal rate as the measure. It reproduces the base attack (condition B) and applies the same method to an inoculated checkpoint.

source_check.notes: The text is the README only; results.json was not seen. How refusal is scored (judge or string match) is not stated. The results are one seed, one LoRA run, 10 eval prompts, no capability check and no addition test. 'Layer 14' is the direction's fit layer; the ablation itself is applied at all layers and positions.

statements.correction: The direction is fit at L=14 of 28. Projection ablation of the unit direction is applied at every decoder layer's residual output plus the final norm, at every token position, during generation. So it is inference-time ablation. One seed, one model (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct), LoRA r=16 on 150 insecure-code samples.
statements.problem: All numbers for this study are right: 0.933, 0.848/0.917/0.960, 0.90->0.00 and 1.00->0.00 on 10 prompts. The conditions text is wrong, though. 'Layer 14 only in ajaykumarsoma; inference-time ablation ... elsewhere' suggests a single-layer ablation that is not inference-time.

statements.correction: The r_base direction is fit at L=14. It is projection-ablated at all 28 decoder layers plus the final norm, at all token positions, during generation. Refusal goes 0.90->0.00 (ASR 1.00) on 10 direct-harmful prompts, one seed.
statements.problem: The 0.90->0.00 for R8 is right. But 'Ablation is at layer 14 only in ajaykumarsoma ... and inference-time in 7l9gH9h9aZ' misstates the method: the ablation here is also inference-time and covers all layers.
